note: Known-answer fixtures for the Designesy scoring engine. Each fixture pins expected verdicts for named checks, and `observed` records what the engine actually returned. A mismatch between expected and observed means the engine changed behavior for a known input — either a regression, or an intentional change whose pin was not yet updated. Fixtures whose name starts with "broken-" are deliberately defective pages; they exist so the corpus can catch a check that stopped detecting something, which a corpus of well-formed pages alone cannot do.

fixtures_detail.name: good-baseline
fixtures_detail.referent: A page that ships the full contract surface: tokens at :root, a reduced-motion block, focus-visible rings, press scale, semantic landmarks.

expectations.why: --paper is declared in :root, which is exactly what v01 looks for.
A :focus-visible rule is present, so the focus check has its primitive.
A @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block is present.
No transition:all anywhere — transitions name their properties.
A forced-colors media query is present.
Exactly one h1 and no skipped levels.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-no-tokens
fixtures_detail.referent: A page with no token layer at all — the shape of an early prototype or a hand-written static page.

expectations.why: No :root block, so --paper cannot resolve. v01 requires the token foundation.
No :focus-visible rule present at all.
No reduced-motion block. Verified behavior: absence is WARN, not FAIL — the reduced-motion check treats omission as a gap rather than a hard break.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-transition-all
fixtures_detail.referent: The single most common CSS performance anti-pattern: transition:all on every interactive element.

expectations.why: transition:all is present in the stylesheet — the exact pattern v11 bans.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-reduced-motion-inverted
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet that opts INTO motion while appearing to support reduced motion — `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` instead of `reduce`.

expectations.why: REGRESSION FIXTURE (caught 2026-09-17). v05 previously matched any @media mentioning prefers-reduced-motion, so `no-preference` — which expresses the opposite intent — passed as readily as `reduce`. That is a false PASS on the accessibility primitive the check exists to verify. Any change that makes this fixture PASS again has reintroduced substring matching on the feature name instead of evaluating its value. Engine 1.1.0 lets a no-preference block PASS when it opts INTO motion (good-reduced-motion-opt-in). This block holds only the reduce kill switch (durations of 0.01ms), which stills motion for users with no preference and leaves it running for users who asked for less, so it must keep reading WARN.

fixtures_detail.name: good-reduced-motion-opt-in
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet that honours reduced motion by making motion opt-in: its animation and transition are declared only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so it ships no reduce block because nothing is left to switch off.

expectations.why: ENGINE 1.1.0 FIX. Motion that exists only under no-preference is never shown to a reduce preference, which is a recommended way to honour it. Engine 1.0.0 read WARN here because it accepted only a reduce block.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-reduced-motion-empty-opt-in
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet with an empty prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block and no reduce block: the shape of a gate that was set up and never filled.

expectations.why: The no-preference block gates nothing, and the animation runs for every user. An empty block must not count as opt-in motion, or the 1.1.0 fix would pass any page that writes the media query and puts nothing in it.

fixtures_detail.name: edge-no-form-fields
fixtures_detail.referent: A content page with no form fields and no input rule in its CSS: a marketing or documentation page, the shape most leaderboard home pages have.

expectations.why: ENGINE 1.1.0 FIX. No field exists for iOS Safari to zoom into, so the 16px floor has nothing to protect. Engine 1.0.0 read WARN here because it had no zero-inputs branch.

fixtures_detail.name: edge-hidden-field-only
fixtures_detail.referent: A page whose only form control is a hidden input (a CSRF or tracking token), with no input rule in its CSS.

expectations.why: A hidden input cannot take focus, so iOS Safari never zooms into it. It must not make the page count as having a field.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-field-without-floor
fixtures_detail.referent: The control for the two fixtures above: the same page keeps its email field, and the CSS still sets no input font-size.

expectations.why: A real email field with no declared 16px floor is the case v27 exists for. The 1.1.0 SKIP applies only when the markup has no field, so this verdict must not move.

fixtures_detail.name: universal-cadence-taste-absent
fixtures_detail.referent: An external site that does not adopt the Designesy Cadence rules: no text-wrap balance or pretty, no tabular-nums, px font sizes. Scored as any external site is (scope=universal).

expectations.why: ENGINE 1.1.0 FIX. v14 restates Designesy Cadence taste. Under scope=universal the absence of a Designesy-specific pattern is SKIP (Tier 2); engine 1.0.0 kept v14 in Tier 1 and read WARN.
ENGINE 1.1.0 FIX. text-wrap balance and pretty are Designesy Cadence taste; their absence on an external site is SKIP under scope=universal. Engine 1.0.0 read WARN.

fixtures_detail.name: contract-cadence-taste-absent
fixtures_detail.referent: The control for the fixture above: the same page scored under scope=contract, the strict mode designesy.org is scored in.

expectations.why: Under scope=contract the Cadence rules are mandatory, so missing ones still WARN. The tier move changes only the universal scope.
Under scope=contract text-wrap balance and pretty are required, so their absence still WARNs.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-reduced-motion-commented-out
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet where the reduced-motion rules exist but are commented out — the shape of a rule disabled during debugging and never restored.

expectations.why: REGRESSION FIXTURE (caught 2026-09-17). Before comments were stripped, a commented-out media query satisfied v05 — the check read CSS text rather than the rules that actually apply. Here the ONLY reduce block is inside a comment, so the page genuinely ships no reduced-motion support and must not PASS. If this fixture starts passing, comment stripping has regressed.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-multiple-h1
fixtures_detail.referent: A page where a template emitted the site name as an h1 in the header and the page title as another h1 in main.

expectations.why: Two h1 elements — v25 tolerates the document but flags the duplicated top level.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-no-heading-outline
fixtures_detail.referent: A client-rendered shell that ships markup with no heading at all — the shape the engine grades when JavaScript would have injected the h1.

expectations.why: No h1 in the delivered markup. Verified behavior: the heading check reports WARN on an absent outline, reserving FAIL for a malformed one. This is still the documented fetch-surface consequence — a JS-injected heading is invisible to a non-executing engine.
Title present, but no landmark and no h1 — the semantic foundation is missing enough parts to FAIL.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-input-zoom
fixtures_detail.referent: Inputs styled below the 16px iOS floor — the shape that causes Safari to auto-zoom on focus and break mobile layout.

expectations.why: An input font-size below the 16px floor is present — this is v27, the iOS auto-zoom trigger. (First written as v16, which is the rem/px scale check; the corpus caught the mix-up on its first run.)

fixtures_detail.name: broken-will-change-everything
fixtures_detail.referent: The blunt performance fix: will-change sprayed onto elements with non-transform properties.

expectations.why: will-change carries properties outside transform/opacity.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-trailing-period
fixtures_detail.referent: Button and label text ending in periods — the copywriting inconsistency v39 targets from Microsoft Fluent guidance.

expectations.why: Button and label text end with a period, which Fluent explicitly forbids.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-bare-noun-buttons
fixtures_detail.referent: Navigation-as-buttons: a marketing header whose buttons are bare nouns rather than verb phrases.

expectations.why: Three bare-noun button labels with no leading verb.

fixtures_detail.name: edge-empty-page
fixtures_detail.referent: A page that returns almost nothing — an error page or an empty deployment. The engine must degrade, not crash.

expectations.why: No title, no meta description, no landmarks — the semantic foundation is entirely absent.
No CSS at all, so no token layer can exist.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-measure-on-non-prose
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet that declares a perfectly good 66ch measure on a decorative container while every paragraph runs unconstrained — the exact shape that passed the old check.

expectations.why: REGRESSION FIXTURE. ch-based rules exist (66ch, 72ch) and both are in the 45-75ch band, so the old text-search implementation returned PASS. Neither selector targets prose — `.spacer` is decorative and `.token-table` is structural. Under the selector-aware check this must WARN: a measure on the wrong element is not a readability fix. If this fixture ever PASSes again, v28 has regressed to pattern-matching on the value.

fixtures_detail.name: good-measure-on-prose
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet that puts the measure where it belongs — on paragraph selectors — which is the state designesy.org was moved to.

expectations.why: The measure is declared on explicit prose selectors (a paragraph descendant combinator, a prose class, a lede class), all in range. This is the counterpart to the fixture above: the check must still PASS when the rule is genuinely applied to prose, or it would be useless as a gate.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-measure-too-wide
fixtures_detail.referent: A stylesheet with the measure on prose but set far too wide — 95ch, well past the readable band.

expectations.why: Prose is constrained, but at 95ch the line length exceeds the 75ch ceiling the check exists to enforce.

fixtures_detail.name: font-aliases-resolve-to-faces
fixtures_detail.referent: A design system that reaches all five of its distinct typefaces through declared :root tokens — the shape next/font produces, and the shape the site itself ships. Five faces behind aliases is genuine typography drift and must be reported as such; the failure mode pinned here is a resolver that skips aliased declarations and reports 0, PASSING a page it never read.

expectations.why: Five distinct faces reached through var() aliases: past the recommended 3, below the >5 FAIL threshold. Counting 0 here means the aliases were skipped rather than resolved — the under-count that passes unread input.

fixtures_detail.name: font-alias-control-five-declared-directly
fixtures_detail.referent: The control for the fixture above: the SAME five faces declared directly, with no token layer. It exists so the aliased fixture cannot pass by having both sides change together.

expectations.why: Five faces declared without any alias layer — the reference reading the aliased fixture must match. If this changes while the aliased one does not, the comparison itself has been lost.

fixtures_detail.name: font-alias-two-hop-chain
fixtures_detail.referent: A two-hop alias chain, which is the shape the live site ships: --sans -> var(--font-sans) -> 'Schibsted Grotesk'. Resolving one level is not enough — the intermediate literal 'var(--font-sans)' would then be attributed as its own family, double-counting one typeface.

expectations.why: Exactly two faces resolve through a two-hop chain, within the recommended three. This is the site's own shape and must keep reading PASS — a resolver returning the intermediate 'var(--font-body)' spelling, or skipping the chain and counting 0, would both be wrong here.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-status-hue-as-text
fixtures_detail.referent: A status hue picked for marks (a dot at 3:1) reused to paint the status word: designesy.org light --warn #b07d04 on --paper #fbfbfc, 2026-10-08.

expectations.why: #b07d04 as text on #fbfbfc measures 3.51:1, under the 4.5:1 body text needs. This is the measured value from the site.
No rule pauses every element, so there is no pause that could hold an entrance.

fixtures_detail.name: good-status-ink-mix
fixtures_detail.referent: The fix designesy.org shipped: a text token per hue, mixed toward the ink in oklab, painted as #7f5e21.

expectations.why: color-mix(in oklab, #b07d04 70%, #1a1a1e) rounds to #7f5e21, which measures 5.76:1 on #fbfbfc; the hue stays on the dot.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-status-hue-dark-scheme
fixtures_detail.referent: A dark scheme declared with prefers-color-scheme whose error red, fine on the light page, falls under contrast on the dark one.

expectations.why: Light: #b91c1c on #ffffff measures 6.47:1. Dark: #991b1b on #0b0b0c measures 2.37:1. Every declared theme is measured, and one failing theme fails the check.

fixtures_detail.name: good-status-hue-large-text
fixtures_detail.referent: A status hue used only for large text (a 2rem verdict heading), where WCAG asks 3:1 instead of 4.5:1.

expectations.why: 3.51:1 is under 4.5:1 but over the 3:1 that 32px text needs, so the same hue that fails as body text passes as a heading.

fixtures_detail.name: broken-paused-entrance
fixtures_detail.referent: designesy.org until 2026-10-08: a site-wide pause holds every animation, and the .fade-up entrance starts at opacity 0, so paused visitors see empty pages.

expectations.why: The pause reaches every element, fadeUp starts at opacity 0, it runs once, and no rule under the pause ends or removes it.
No status color is used as text on this page.

fixtures_detail.name: good-paused-entrance-ended
fixtures_detail.referent: The fix designesy.org shipped: under the pause, each entrance gets a negative delay longer than itself, so it holds on its last frame.

expectations.why: -3600s is longer than the 600ms entrance, so under the pause it sits on its last frame, at opacity 1.

fixtures_detail.name: edge-no-pause-scope
fixtures_detail.referent: The common case: an entrance from opacity 0 and a reduced-motion block that shortens animations, with no rule that pauses them.

expectations.why: Nothing sets animation-play-state: paused, so no entrance can be held; shortening an animation runs it to its end.
